observed_problem: v0.01 defines evaluation but does not fully govern recursive self-improvement or prevent post-result goalpost movement.
root_cause: No frozen successor contract, experiment registry, or permanent regression-memory requirement.
hypothesis: Pre-registration plus independent evaluation and regression preservation will make recursive improvement auditable and resistant to self-serving metric changes.
proposed_change: Add controlled recursive lifecycle, frozen release contract, improvement/experiment ledgers, regression corpus, anti-gaming rules, and independent promotion gate.
preregistered_acceptance: v0.02 defines a frozen successor contract mechanism
v0.02 prohibits candidate self-certification
v0.02 requires adopted fixes to produce regression memory
v0.02 preserves v0.01 critical evaluation invariants
result: The v0.03 recursive cycle successfully used frozen criteria, independent-role verification, regression preservation, and append-only events; however v0.02's own historical release evidence remains incomplete.
disposition: Retain recursive governance; do not retroactively promote v0.02.

observed_problem: Core records are machine-readable but only manually validated; malformed and semantically inconsistent artifacts can silently enter the workspace.
root_cause: v0.02 defines schemas/governance but no executable validation layer.
hypothesis: A deterministic CLI/library that validates schemas plus core semantic invariants will reject seeded invalid artifacts while accepting valid fixtures.
proposed_change: Build a Python validator for JSON/JSONL, schemas, stable IDs, duplicate IDs, references, event lifecycles, contracts, regressions, metrics, snapshots, and manifests.
preregistered_acceptance: 100% of preregistered invalid fixtures are rejected
100% of preregistered valid fixtures are accepted
all validator automated tests pass
result: Validator CLI/library and 30-test suite passed; 22/22 invalid fixture classes rejected and 4/4 valid fixture classes accepted.
disposition: Adopt in v0.03; preserve executable regression coverage.

observed_problem: Frozen release criteria depend on external manifest hashing and the contract schema does not encode an integrity mechanism or rollback/failure conditions.
root_cause: The v1 frozen-contract schema was intentionally minimal and cannot mechanically protect the full recursive release contract.
hypothesis: Embedding a canonical contract hash and validating it against the manifest will detect post-freeze mutation.
proposed_change: Define frozen-contract schema v2 with explicit requirements, gates, failure/promotion/rollback fields and canonical SHA-256 integrity validation.
preregistered_acceptance: all mutation fixtures are rejected
unmodified v0.03 frozen contract passes integrity verification
result: Canonical frozen-contract SHA-256 validation passed; mutation fixture is rejected; manifest contract-hash mismatch is rejected.
disposition: Adopt in v0.03; preserve executable regression coverage.

observed_problem: v0.02 requires metric reconciliation but provides no executable denominator/snapshot semantics.
root_cause: Metric records and denominator snapshots have prose requirements but no schemas or cross-record validator.
hypothesis: Explicit snapshot/metric schemas plus cutoff/scope/denominator reconciliation rules will prevent missing data, denominator drift, and mismatched scope from being reported as valid metrics.
proposed_change: Add denominator-snapshot and metric-ledger schemas and semantic reconciliation checks.
preregistered_acceptance: valid reconciled metrics pass
missing denominator, missing snapshot, cutoff mismatch, scope mismatch, and calculation mismatch fixtures fail
result: Metric/snapshot reconciliation is executable and catches missing denominator, missing snapshot, cutoff/scope/denominator/calculation/source-reference mismatches.
disposition: Adopt in v0.03; preserve executable regression coverage.

observed_problem: No-self-certification and governed regression retirement are manual rules only.
root_cause: Release scorecards, governance decisions, and retirement relationships lack executable schemas and cross-checks.
hypothesis: Machine-checking evaluator identity and retirement decisions will catch self-certification and silent critical regression removal where the records make these violations observable.
proposed_change: Add release-scorecard and decision schemas plus semantic checks for evaluator separation and governed retirement.
preregistered_acceptance: self-certification fixture fails
retired regression without an existing governance decision fails
valid independently evaluated scorecard passes
result: Candidate self-certification and ungoverned regression retirement are mechanically rejected when records expose the violation.
disposition: Adopt in v0.03; preserve executable regression coverage.
Adopt deterministic LINT-001..LINT-010 layer as v0.04 experimental capability.
hypothesis: A deterministic, context-aware linter will detect preregistered specification defects with zero seeded clean-case false positives.
observed_problem: Structural validation cannot detect weak natural-language specifications such as vague requirements, missing acceptance criteria, or unverified requirements.
preregistered_acceptance: 50/50 seeded defect cases detect their expected rule
50/50 seeded clean cases emit zero findings
all emitted corpus findings are expected
all findings contain exact span and rationale
proposed_change: Implement LINT-001 through LINT-010 with exact-span diagnostics, deterministic ordering, CLI/library access, and a frozen clean/defect corpus.
result: Frozen corpus passed: 50/50 defect cases detected, 50/50 clean cases accepted, finding precision 1.0, diagnostic completeness 1.0.
root_cause: v0.03 validates artifact shape and cross-record integrity but intentionally has no specification-quality lint layer.

disposition: Retain context exclusions and clean-counterexample guardrails.
hypothesis: Context exclusion plus clean-spec counterexamples and per-rule precision guardrails will prevent this failure mode from recurring in the linter.
observed_problem: Rule engines can create costly false positives when they ignore textual context or confuse examples with active requirements.
preregistered_acceptance: all 50 clean counterexamples pass
minimum per-rule precision is 1.0 on frozen corpus
REG-0004 continues to pass
proposed_change: Ignore fenced code, blockquotes, Notes/Rationale commentary for active lint rules and require clean counterexamples for every rule.
result: All 50 clean counterexamples passed and every rule achieved precision 1.0 on the frozen corpus.
root_cause: Broad syntactic heuristics without context classification can reject valid inputs.

disposition: Adopt release snapshots and historical prefix verification; preserve as REG-0005.
hypothesis: Preserving the release-time package manifest as a version-local snapshot and validating the historical byte prefix for known append-only ledgers will retain tamper detection without making future appends invalidate prior releases.
observed_problem: Historical v0.03 manifest verification fails after legitimate successor appends to shared append-only JSONL ledgers.
preregistered_acceptance: legitimate post-v0.03 append passes old manifest verification
mutation within the v0.03 historical prefix fails
immutable version-local mutation still fails
existing manifest mismatch regressions remain passing
proposed_change: Add historical package-snapshot prefix verification for append-only shared ledgers while keeping exact hashes for immutable artifacts.
result: Historical v0.03 release verification passes after successor changes using append-prefix verification and release snapshots; mutation scenarios fail as required.
root_cause: v0.03 manifest verification treats all content hashes as whole-file immutable, while the recursive protocol intentionally uses append-only shared ledgers across versions and records no version-local snapshot reference in the manifest itself.

disposition: Adopt deterministic traceability engine in v0.05; retain experimental release classification until independent real-project effectiveness evidence exists.
hypothesis: A deterministic typed traceability graph will detect broken, semantically invalid, cyclic, and incomplete critical delivery chains while supporting exact impact analysis.
observed_problem: Spec Creator can validate identifiers and lint specification prose, but it cannot prove that a critical requirement is connected through implementation and verification artifacts to a release gate.
preregistered_acceptance: all frozen invalid graphs detected
all frozen valid and impact graphs accepted
all critical requirements in accepted graphs have complete traceability
all impact sets exactly match preregistration
all emitted invalid-case diagnostic codes are preregistered for their cases
proposed_change: Add a versioned Goal→Requirement→Feature→Task→Test→Gate graph validator and impact analyzer with a hash-locked synthetic evaluation corpus.
result: Frozen v0.05 evaluation passed: 20/20 invalid graphs detected, 10/10 valid+impact graphs accepted, 10/10 critical requirements complete, 5/5 impact cases exact, and diagnostic precision 1.0.
root_cause: Existing cross-reference checks establish identifier existence but not a typed, complete delivery relationship graph.

disposition: Retry product hypothesis under v0.06.1 without changing semantic cases or metric thresholds.
hypothesis: A bounded trace-aware ambiguity engine will intercept at least 80% of preregistered implementation-time clarification triggers while keeping unnecessary questions at or below 5%.
observed_problem: Spec Creator can lint weak prose and validate traceability, but it cannot classify which unresolved ambiguities need an owner question or prioritize those questions by delivery impact.
preregistered_acceptance: defect detection >= 0.95
decision-needed accuracy >= 0.95
priority top-question accuracy >= 0.90
clarification interception proxy >= 0.80
unnecessary question rate <= 0.05
critical ambiguity escape count = 0
proposed_change: Add deterministic ambiguity taxonomy, resolution classification, traceability-linked priority, question generation, and a hash-locked clarification-interception proxy.
result: Frozen v0.06 evaluation dependency failed before governed implementation: all 16 embedded trace graphs violated the inherited v0.05 schema.
root_cause: Existing controls detect selected specification defects but do not model ambiguity resolution state or question cost.

hypothesis: With parent-valid preregistration and final package sealing, the same bounded ambiguity engine can meet the original v0.06 effectiveness thresholds while preserving inherited integrity controls.
observed_problem: The ambiguity-engine product gap remains after v0.06 was blocked by an invalid evaluation dependency; shipping-manifest sequencing also lacks executable protection.
preregistered_acceptance: same original v0.06 product thresholds
16/16 graph-backed cases parent-valid before freeze
REG-0001 through REG-0009 pass
final live package manifest validates with zero errors/warnings
proposed_change: Retry the unchanged ambiguity semantics under a parent-valid frozen corpus, add pre-freeze dependency validation and final package-manifest enforcement, then evaluate the same clarification-interception proxy.
root_cause: v0.06 preregistration did not validate embedded artifacts with parent executable controls, and final package manifest generation occurred too early in prior cycles.
